2023.10.14 15:08:47 +0530 petition/application filed for compensation on account of the fatal injuries sustained by Sh. Raghubir Singh in a road vehicular accident which took place on 29.05.1998 at about 04:30 pm at Near Sojat City High School, Pali, Rajasthan on National Highway No.14.
CASE OF THE PETITIONER SIDE 2.
Succinctly, the case put forth vide petition/application is that deceased Sh. Raghubir Singh was employed as driver on truck bearing registration number HR- 46/7571.
The respondent no.01 was employed as 2nd driver on same truck on the day of incident i.e. 29.05.1998.
The respondent no.01 was driving the truck and the deceased was taking rest.
At about 04:30 pm, their truck reached near Sojat City High School, Pali, Rajasthan on National Highway No.14.
The respondent no.01 was driving the truck in rash and negligent manner and in high speed.
The respondent no.01 could not control the truck due to high speed and applied sudden brakes.
Due to same, deceased who was sitting on front seat fell down and came under the wheels of the truck.
He died at the spot.

The police did not investigate the matter properly and registered the case against the respondent no.03 as driver of the offending vehicle at the time of incident whereas actually the respondent no.01 was driving the said truck at the time of incident.

The respondent no.02 who is the owner of offending vehicle has responded to the notice served under Section 133 of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as M. V. Act) stating respondent no.01 to be his 2nd driver and driving the offending truck at the time of incident.
Postmortem of the deceased was conducted at General Hospital, Sojat City, District Pali, Smt. Mukesh & Ors.
Vs. Inderjit Singh & Ors.
MACT No.76802/2016 Page No.4 of 10

Deceased was aged about 35 years at the time of accident and was earning handsomely.
Petitioner no.01 is wife of the deceased.
Petitioner no.02 to 04 are children of the deceased.
Petitioner no.04 was minor at the time of incident.
The respondent no.05 is mother of the deceased.
All the petitioners and respondent no.05 were dependent upon the deceased.

9.3 No final submissions were made on behalf of respondent no.01, 02, 03 and 05.
DISCUSSION 10.

Before proceeding further to decide the matter on the merits of this case, it would be apposite to first decide the issue of maintainability of present petition raised by the respondent no.04 in this matter.
It is the case of the petitioners themselves that the deceased Raghubir Singh was employed as driver on truck in question.
It is also the case of the petitioners themselves that the respondent no.01 was another driver of the vehicle in question.

The case of petitioner side qua respondent no.01 being the driver of vehicle in question on the date and time of incident is questionable considering the stand of respondent no.01 vide his written statement and in view of the final report of Investigating Agency, the certified records of which have been filed by petitioner side itself.
Even if we leave the said aspect aside, it is not in dispute that respondent no.01 or 03 whosoever was driving was also employee of the owner/respondent no.02.
It is not the case of petitioners that some other vehicle(s) was/were involved in the incident.
Instead it is the case of petitioners themselves that the incident took place when the deceased and the driver/helper of the vehicle in question were traveling in the given vehicle only.
In these circumstances, deceased cannot be said to be third party to the respondent no.02/owner of the vehicle in question.

The petitioners have not mentioned as to under which provision they have filed the application for grant of compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-
as demanded vide prayer clause 'A' of the petition/application.
Smt. Mukesh & Ors. Vs. Inderjit Singh & Ors.

Though, the petitioners have prayed for grant of interim compensation of Rs.50,000/- vide prayer clause 'B' of their petition/application, however, they have sought said interim compensation under Section 140 M. V. Act.
The repealed Section 140 M. V. Act earlier provided for grant of compensation in certain cases on principle of no fault liability.
The new corresponding section for grant of compensation without proving rashness/negligence in driving which exists as on date is section 164 M. V. Act.

Both general petition/application for grant of compensation under Section 166 M. V. Act or for grant of compensation without proving rash and negligence in the driving of vehicle under Section 164 M. V. Act are maintainable only where the injured/deceased/victim is third party to the vehicle in question.
The provisions for grant of compensation under Section 166 M. V. Act and 164 M. V. Act (erstwhile Section 140 M. V. Act) can not be invoked against own vehicle and its insurer.

Reliance can be placed upon the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Smt Mukesh vs Shri Inderjit Singh on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47845974/
